purpose: Evaluate whether exact asynchronous up/down weight I/O, including an io_uring or O_DIRECT bounded-buffer design, can be a 10 tok/s path under the current 16GB cgroup and accepted vendor DeepSeek SOTA.

touch_split_observation.interpretation: The diagnostic shows cold page touch/refault dominates raw CPU fallback, but the synchronous touch/profile run itself regresses to 2.6 tok/s and fails the accepted TTFT gate. It is only a bottleneck diagnostic, not a performance route.

async_io_budget.assumption: Grant a best-case exact design where all up/down CPU dot work costs only the touch-split after-touch fallback time, and all other non-up/down decode work remains at the accepted SOTA bound.

dependency_window_analysis.exact_prefetch_window: Selected experts for layer L are known only after that layer's router/selection graph. An exact active up-source read cannot be issued for the next token or future layer before those selections exist.
dependency_window_analysis.consequence: Most up-source read latency is on the critical path unless the design falls back to static/hotset prediction, which is the already-closed topN payload frontier.

dependency_window_analysis.exact_prefetch_window: Down source can be requested after selected experts are known and while gate/up work is executing.
dependency_window_analysis.consequence: The touch-split decode up fallback-after-touch time is only about 1463 ms total, so it cannot hide the roughly 20915 ms down touch/page-read diagnostic cost or the 156.47 GiB active-source byte frontier.

dependency_window_analysis.exact_prefetch_window: The 16GB cgroup is already at memory_peak=16000000000 with about 15.1GB file cache. Buffered prefetch competes with the accepted page-cache shape; O_DIRECT avoids page cache but must still move the same bytes through bounded host buffers.
dependency_window_analysis.consequence: The previous current-path WILLNEED negative control reduced some faults but regressed to 4.0 tok/s, and broad/current-tensor page advice remains rejected.

decision.reason: A best-case exact active-I/O design has only about 3.94s of unhidden I/O budget after charging non-up/down decode and after-touch CPU fallback. It would require 17.8-39.7 GiB/s effective unhidden bandwidth, far above the measured 3.04 GiB/s gate-pack O_DIRECT prefill path, and active up-source reads have too little exact dependency window to hide. Buffered page prefetch has already regressed under the 16GB cgroup.
allowed_reopen_conditions: A new representation reduces active up/down source bytes by several times while preserving exactness or fixed-text correctness.
A new measured storage path demonstrates at least 17.8 GiB/s effective unhidden bandwidth inside the strict 16GB cgroup with no page-cache regression.
A different model/artifact reduces routed expert bytes or selected expert count and passes correctness.
decision.next_executable_route: Continue only with a new hard-bound artifact that changes bytes/coverage, or obtain explicit disk cleanup approval for full alternate GGUF empirical testing.
